topics.title: Introduction to Financial Accounting and Double Entry System

subtopics.content: 1.1 - 2.8 History, accounting process, source documents, subsidiary books, ledgers, cash books, trial balance, bank reconciliation, suspense accounts
subtopics.objective: Understand accounting nature, users, and qualitative characteristics[cite: 261]; apply accounting equations and double entry principles[cite: 261]; post source documents to prime entry books and ledgers[cite: 261]; prepare single/double/three-column cash books, petty cash books, and Trial Balances[cite: 261]; prepare Bank Reconciliation Statements and correct errors via Suspense Accounts[cite: 261, 262].

topics.title: Accounting Concepts, Sole Trader Final Accounts, Provisions, Reserves, and Manufacturing Accounts

subtopics.content: 3.1 - 6.3 Accounting concepts, Trading/P&L/Balance Sheet adjustments, provisions for bad debts, depreciation methods, reserves, manufacturing accounts
subtopics.objective: Identify accounting concepts and limitations[cite: 262]; prepare sole proprietor Trading, Profit & Loss Accounts, and Balance Sheets with adjustments (accruals, prepayments)[cite: 262]; calculate bad debt provisions and depreciation (straight line, reducing balance, sum of digits, revaluation)[cite: 262]; prepare Manufacturing Accounts classifying prime cost, factory overheads, and work-in-progress[cite: 262].

topics.title: Control Accounts, Incomplete Records, Not-For-Profit Accounts, Partnership, Company, VAT, and Departmental/Branch Accounts

subtopics.content: 7.1 - 13.5 Control ledgers, single entry conversion, non-profit accounts, partnership final accounts/goodwill, company share issue/ratios/cash flow, VAT returns, branch accounting
subtopics.objective: Prepare Sales and Purchases Ledger Control Accounts[cite: 262]; convert incomplete records using markup/margin to final accounts[cite: 262]; prepare Receipts/Payments, Income & Expenditure Accounts, and Accumulated Funds[cite: 263]; account for partnership appropriation, capital/current accounts, partner admission, goodwill, and dissolution[cite: 263]; prepare company accounts, financial ratios, and Cash Flow Statements[cite: 263]; compute Input/Output VAT returns[cite: 263]; prepare Departmental and Branch Accounts[cite: 263, 264].

topics.title: Public Sector Accounting, IT in Accounting, Miscellaneous Accounts, and Financial System

subtopics.content: 14.1 - 17.6 Public sector revenue/expenditure, computerized accounting systems, Joint Venture, Consignment, Contract, Hire Purchase, money/capital markets
subtopics.objective: Distinguish public and private sector accounting and prepare simple government accounts[cite: 264]; compare manual and computerized accounting systems[cite: 264]; prepare Joint Venture, Consignment, Contract, and Hire Purchase Accounts[cite: 264]; analyze money/capital markets, share offer methods, capital market regulations, and investor benefits[cite: 264].
